27:
28:`EXIT = {GREEN: 0, RED: 1, ERROR: 2}`, and the verdict text always agrees with the code. A
29:normal run exits the worst verdict any enabled check returned. `--selftest` exits `0` when every
30:fixture matched, `1` when any fixture missed, and `2` when `fixtures/` is absent or empty — a
31:gate with no known-bad is not a gate. `--capabilities` and `--help` exit `0`.

34:|---|---|---|
35:| `g1-surface-fetch-integrity` | a page came back short (<500B) / markerless / hash-mismatched | zero pages, the manifest is missing or unparseable, or the index did not return 200 |

37:| `g3-snapshot-freshness` | newest snapshot >8 days old — the weekly loop stopped | no snapshot at all |

1:# NEGATIVE_EVIDENCE — dead-end ledger
2:
3:> Refuted hypotheses, reverted "wins", NO-SHIP measurements, exhausted veins. Read this BEFORE
4:> starting any perf/detector/optimization hypothesis. Format + doctrine: the
5:> `negative-evidence-ledger` skill. A RED loop tick counts as processed only if it appends an
6:> entry here (enforced: `loop-kit/neg-evidence-gate.sh` — see gate wiring in AGENTS.md §4).
7:
8:## NE-1 — `Accept: text/markdown` on docs.x.ai returns 404, not markdown
9:
10:- **Date:** 2026-09-10 · **Level:** measured, reproduced
11:- **Hypothesis:** the polite thing for a markdown fetcher is to advertise
12:  `Accept: text/markdown, text/plain`, since `llms.txt` says every page is available as markdown.
13:- **Result:** REFUTED. With that header, `https://docs.x.ai/grok-bot/overview.md` returns **404**
14:  with a 411-byte body; all 18 Grok Bot pages did. `Accept: */*` and `Accept: text/plain` return
15:  200. Proven with both `curl` and `urllib` on the same URL in the same minute.
16:- **Why it matters:** the first snapshot recorded 0/18 pages OK and *still wrote a manifest*. Had
17:  the gate not treated an empty OK-set as ERROR, the repo would have frozen 18 error pages as "the
18:  Grok Bot surface" and reported "no change" every week thereafter.
19:- **Retry condition:** re-test only if `docs.x.ai` publishes a content-negotiation contract, or if
20:  `llms.txt` starts documenting an `Accept` header that is proven to work. Until then the header is
21:  pinned in `bin/gb-surface-snapshot.py` with a do-not-improve comment.
22:
23:## NE-2 — private-network reach for Grok Bot computers is not available on this account
24:
25:- **Date:** 2026-09-10 · **Level:** docs-verified + client-binary-verified
26:- **Hypothesis (from ecosystem research):** tunnel Joshua's Tailscale tailnet onto the Grok Bot
27:  cloud computer so Bots can reach Studio/Brain services directly.
28:- **Result:** NO-SHIP. The vendor pattern exists but runs through **Team Setup, which is Enterprise
29:  only** (<https://docs.x.ai/grok-bot/private-networks>), and this account measures
30:  `stripeMembershipStatus: ultra`, `isEnterpriseUser: false`. The client agrees: `sand_network_controls`,
31:  `sand_box_egress_tunnel`, and `team_*` gates are all **disabled**. Grok Bot also has no on-prem or
32:  BYO-image deployment (<https://docs.x.ai/grok-bot/security> § hosting).
33:- **Retry condition:** `deployment/<date>.json` → `account.is_enterprise_user` becomes `true`, or
34:  `gates.enabled_names` gains `sand_network_controls` / `sand_box_egress_tunnel`. The weekly audit
35:  detects both automatically; `g6` will surface the delta.
36:
37:## NE-3 — a name-based feature-gate diff is not an entitlement signal
38:
39:- **Date:** 2026-09-11 · **Level:** measured, classified against the live payload
40:- **Hypothesis:** comparing the set of *named* enabled Statsig gates between two audits tells us
41:  what xAI turned on or off for this account.

# /fh — grade a repo against the FrankenSuite rigor oracles, one product finding per pass

> **The rule this skill exists to enforce:** a rigor pass that ends in a document scored ZERO
> (Rule Zero). Every pass names exactly one gap, proves it live, and either closes it in the
> product or halts with the one human decision blocking it. Measured 2026-08-21: 80% of files
> touched in 14 days were documents; an Apple app accumulated a Charter, a Successor-Plan, and
> adoption receipts and zero app. This skill is the antibody.

## THREE ORACLES — all independent, none self-graded

| Oracle | Command | What it grades | Ceiling |
|---|---|---|---|
| **L1–L7 layer stack** | `fh rigor` | the seven artifact-rigor layers, each with pinned verbatim exemplars from Jeff's repos (`frankengraphdb@a3c2bec…`, `asupersync@c83dff8…`, `frankentui@e6fc3c6…`, `frankensim@4200810…`) | 7 layers / 17 exemplars |
| **62 mechanical checks** | `~/Developer/foundry/flywheel/stamp-check.sh --repo <path>` | byte/structure presence of a LIVE process (AGENTS.md §0/§4, beads, hooks, drivers, registries, ledgers) — "no vibes, no LLM judgment calls" | **clearbill = 48 PASS / 3 FAIL** — the proven-reachable corpus ceiling |
| **9 measured standards** | `fh standards check --json` + read `~/Developer/franken-harvest/standards/*.md` | doctrine each distilled from a failure we already PAID for, with path+quote+line | stamped = `code:PASS` + matching `payload_content_id` |

**Why three:** each catches what the others cannot. `stamp-check` is blind to whether a gate
is *valuable* (fh `value-bearing-gates.md` is not); `fh rigor` is blind to whether the
mechanism is *installed* (stamp-check is not); `standards check` only says the doctrine is
present, not obeyed. A repo is graded only when all three have run. **An oracle that did not
run is `NOT_RUN`, never implied-green** (fh `causal-known-bads.md`).

## ⛔ PRE-FLIGHT — what is measured, refuse to grade without it

```bash
fh --info | grep -iE 'build|revision'  # installed binary at or after the source HEAD you rely on?
fh doctor --json | head -20            # corpus live? executable identity? scheduler wired?
fh standards check --json              # stamped? (STANDARDS_NOT_STAMPED = stamp FIRST, grade second)
git -C <repo> rev-parse HEAD           # pin the revision every finding cites
```

12:FH currently has three lifecycles that are coupled more tightly than their contracts require:

18:The coupling is safe but over-broad. `build.rs` hashes `src`, `tests`, `standards`, dependency manifests, and release scripts into one source-tree identity. 29:- after a separately authorized local-mirror mutation, an operator or authorized caller may invoke the one-shot `fh refresh --trigger manual`; v1 installs no event, schedule, cron, launchd, or watcher integration.
30:
31:A native binary rebuild remains mandatory when executable behavior changes and the new behavior is wanted. Mirror HEAD movement, ledger/document/bead movement, and ordinary generation aging never require a rebuild by themselves.

10:## Executive summary
11:
12:FH currently has three lifecycles that are coupled more tightly than their contracts require:
13:
14:1. the native executable and its exact build provenance;
15:2. mutable evidence/search/document generations derived from the local mirror and ledger;
16:3. long-running MCP reader processes that load one generation.
17:
18:The coupling is safe but over-broad. `build.rs` hashes `src`, `tests`, `standards`, dependency manifests, and release scripts into one source-tree identity. The technical cache includes that identity in its key. Doctor compares an active daily generation's producer tree identity to the running binary by exact equality. MCP refuses when loaded input bytes move and asks for a restart. Those mechanisms prove exact provenance, but they also turn data-only movement and unrelated source changes into binary-currentness or process-restart work.
19:
20:This plan separates the lifecycles without weakening provenance:
21:
22:- the installed binary remains immutable between real executable releases;
23:- a new native `fh refresh` coordinator rebuilds only dirty data legs with that installed binary;
24:- exact producer source/executable identities remain recorded for audit;
25:- narrower per-surface contract identities decide reader/writer compatibility;
26:- one immutable refresh bundle names a coherent set of component generations and advances through one atomic pointer;
27:- MCP reloads a compatible active bundle at request boundaries without fetching, building, or mutating state;
28:- doctor distinguishes input movement, generation currency, binary compatibility, and trigger policy;
29:- after a separately authorized local-mirror mutation, an operator or authorized caller may invoke the one-shot `fh refresh --trigger manual`; v1 installs no event, schedule, cron, launchd, or watcher integration.
30:
31:A native binary rebuild remains mandatory when executable behavior changes and the new behavior is wanted. Mirror HEAD movement, ledger/document/bead movement, and ordinary generation aging never require a rebuild by themselves.
32:
33:## Goals, non-goals, and success metrics

39:| REQ-001 | Refresh data with the installed binary | A mirror-only fixture change moves the active bundle and buyer-visible result while the installed executable SHA-256 remains byte-id

def command_requires_remote(argv: Sequence[str]) -> bool:
    if not argv:
        return False
    basenames = [os.path.basename(value) for value in argv]
    if "release-build" in basenames:
        return True
    command_index = 0
    if basenames[0] == "env":
        command_index = 1
        while command_index < len(argv):
            value = argv[command_index]
            if "=" not in value or value.startswith("="):
                break
            command_index += 1
    return (
